result:
There's something quietly astonishing about the fact that every person you pass on the street is carrying an entire universe behind their eyes. The woman waiting at the crosswalk is mentally rehearsing a difficult conversation. The man walking his dog is remembering his father teaching him to whistle. Somewhere, someone is deciding to forgive someone else, right now, and no one will ever write it down.

I find this thought both humbling and comforting. We move through crowds like planets through solar systems — gravitationally connected, yet each following our own private orbit. The sheer scale of human experience happening simultaneously defies comprehension. Right now, someone is falling in love for the first time. Someone is saying goodbye at a hospital bed. Someone is tasting mango for the first time. Someone is laughing so hard they can't breathe.

And yet we so often reduce each other to silhouettes — the rude driver, the slow cashier, the noisy neighbor. It's a kind of poverty of imagination, and I'm as guilty of it as anyone. But when I remember that every stranger is the protagonist of a story I'll never hear, something softens. Patience becomes easier. Curiosity becomes natural.

Maybe that's the whole task of being human: to hold onto the awareness that other people are real. Not props in our story, but authors of their own. The world would be gentler if we practiced this more — this quiet, radical act of remembering everyone else's interiority. Perhaps kindness is just attention, paid deliberately.
